step1_summary.Chief complaint: Right knee pain and clicking for about two weeks, worsened with running and certain movements.

Symptoms.Severity: Pain worsens after around 2.5-3 miles of running, causing patient to stop
Symptoms.Aggravating factors: Running (especially after 2.5-3 miles), gym exercises involving knee flexion and extension (e.g., abs work)
Symptoms.Alleviating factors: Ice reduces swelling, currently no pain at rest or when sitting
Symptoms.Other symptoms: Occasional clicking in the knee, mild swelling initially but no current swelling, one episode of right toe tingling after running, mild pitting leg edema (indentations from socks) after standing

step1_summary.Past medical history: Far-sightedness with LASIK surgery, history of UTI/kidney stone episode, occasional joint issues in past (rare), no known chronic joint diseases
step1_summary.Medications/allergies: Occasional Ibuprofen (max 400 mg), Vitamin D, Melatonin, Aleve (likely naproxen or acetaminophen), occasional Xanax, smokes marijuana sometimes, no allergies mentioned
step1_summary.Family/social history: No mention of family joint diseases or other hereditary conditions; physically active, training for marathon, plays sports including ice hockey, recent ice fall with a bruise months ago
step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: No fever, no persistent swelling or redness currently, full range of motion, no locking, no knee instability reported, no calf pain, mild intermittent pitting edema in legs especially after standing, no changes in skin colour or temperature in legs

V: Venous insufficiency causing mild lower leg edema: Patient notes pitting edema (sock indentation) after standing, no redness or pain which decrease likelihood of DVT.
Vascular claudication unlikely but tingling in toes raises minor vascular concern.
I: Reactive or low-grade knee synovitis or bursitis post minor injury or overuse, possibly inflammatory in nature.
Post-injury mild inflammation from previous ice hockey fall.
N: Unlikely tumor/neoplasm given acute symptoms and absence of mass/swelling.
D: Early degenerative knee changes or overuse injury such as patellofemoral pain syndrome or meniscal irritation due to recent increased running.
Muscle or ligament strain or minor cartilage damage given increased load from marathon training.
I2: Possible mild NSAID-related issues but no evidence of toxicity or iatrogenic cause.
C: No congenital abnormalities reported or suspected.
A: Low likelihood of autoimmune arthritis given no other joint involvement, no morning stiffness or systemic symptoms.
T: Traumatic injury from ice hockey fall several months ago may have predisposed to current symptoms, or new minor running-related microtrauma.
Possible ligament or meniscal injury causing pain and clicking.
E: No endocrine or metabolic causes clearly suggested by transcript; no mention of diabetes or neuropathy to explain tingling toes.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Overuse Injury with possible Meniscal Irritation or Patellofemoral Syndrome
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Recent increase in running mileage and training for marathon with onset of right knee pain and clicking after 2-3 miles, pain on flexion/extension, history of minor knee trauma months ago makes overuse injury and meniscal irritation most probable.
supporting_evidence: Clicking sensation in knee during flexion-extension
No locking or instability but some mild swelling initially
History of minor trauma (bruise from ice hockey fall)
opposing_evidence: No mechanical locking or giving way

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Some swelling initially, symptom improvement with ice and NSAIDs, pain pattern consistent with inflammatory response to minor injury or overuse; however no warmth or redness or systemic symptoms present.
supporting_evidence: Initial mild swelling responsive to ice
Pain intermittent and related to activity
Use of NSAIDs provides some symptom relief
opposing_evidence: No fever, no persistent swelling or redness
Symptoms localized and no other joints involved

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Mild Peripheral Neuropathy or Nerve Irritation
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Tingling in toes once after run could be nerve irritation due to mechanical stress or mild neuropathy, rare but plausible given localized and transient nature.
supporting_evidence: Single episode of right toe tingling after running

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Venous Insufficiency or Mild Peripheral Edema
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Mild leg edema after standing suggests some venous insufficiency but no signs of DVT or serious vascular disease; unlikely to explain knee pain or clicking.
supporting_evidence: Sock indentation noted after prolonged standing
No redness, warmth or calf pain
opposing_evidence: No swelling in knee or redness
No vascular changes like color or temperature alteration

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Ligamentous Injury (e.g., partial ACL or MCL strain)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: History of ice hockey injury months ago could have caused ligament damage but symptoms stabilized and the primary complaint is pain and clicking without instability or locking. ACL tear usually has instability.
supporting_evidence: History of trauma with fall on ice
opposing_evidence: No episodes of giving way or instability
Full range of motion with no locking or inability to straighten knee
